clue.text: Join lowest paid, briefly in difficulties

indicators.note: something in difficulties is in a mess, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: PD is the short form of paid, as on a receipt

explanation.surface: A complaint that the worst-paid workers are struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in difficulties' shuffles LOWEST with PD (paid, shortened) to give the welding term; 'Join' looks like a verb about workers but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot-weld is a joint made by welding at small points, so it is a kind of join.

clue.text: Portico constructed in far from amateur fashion

parts.note: a professional is the opposite of an amateur
style means fashion

explanation.surface: A porch built with professional skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A prostyle is a classical portico with columns standing in front of the building.

clue.text: Crisis occurring in entrance to side street?

definitions.meaning: a decisive moment when things change
a place where a driver turns off into a side road

explanation.surface: An emergency happening at the mouth of a little road.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a critical moment, and literally the place one turns.

clue.text: One offers motion from the floor, to make progress

definitions.text: One offers motion from the floor, to make progress

parts.words: One offers motion from the floor, to make progress
parts.note: reads like a delegate proposing from the conference floor, but it is a machine that carries you up from storey to storey

explanation.surface: A speaker at a meeting putting forward a motion to advance business.
explanation.definitionFit: A lift carries people up from one floor to another, moving them upward.

clue.text: Lower status of qualification, not entirely without notice

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first part goes around the notice
the word is not given in full, losing its last letter

parts.note: a degree is an academic qualification
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Downgrading a diploma partly, without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside; 'not entirely' drops a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade someone is to reduce their rank or standing.

clue.text: Joey possibly has caged bird — almost 18th century style

indicators.note: caging holds something inside, so the bird goes within

parts.note: a joey is a young kangaroo, a roo

indicators.note: almost means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: a cock is a male bird

explanation.surface: A pet kangaroo kept with a caged bird, in an ornate old style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts COCK to COC, which ROO 'has caged'. A joey is a baby kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the ornate decorative style of 18th-century Europe.

clue.text: Opposed to article, the very thing that should be brought up

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read upward, reversed

parts.note: 'it' means the very thing, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: Objecting to an essay that ought to be raised for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses IT to TI under AN.
explanation.definitionFit: To be anti something is to be against it, opposed.

clue.text: Jaw with man taking new offer up

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read upward, reversed

parts.note: a bid is an offer

explanation.surface: Someone speaks to a man who accepts a fresh proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaw' looks like a verb, to chat, but is the bone; 'up' reverses only the offer, and 'taking' means containing.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandible is the lower jawbone.

clue.text: Being obsessively concerned about first person's reference

definitions.text: Being obsessively concerned about first person's reference

parts.words: Being obsessively concerned about first person's reference
parts.note: the first person is 'I', the self, so an obsessive concern with oneself is described

explanation.surface: A description of someone fixated on talking about themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive preoccupation with the self is the textbook sense of this word for vanity run wild.

clue.text: Piano that we have to drop, when it's heavy

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft
what we have is ours, so OUR

explanation.surface: Movers deciding to let go of a heavy piano they own.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'drop' something done to the piano; it is really rain falling heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain that falls heavily is said to pour, a downpour of drops.

clue.text: I won't answer for this — what a shame you'll get caught!

indicators.note: being caught means being held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: said in consolation, 'never mind' is like 'what a pity, don't worry'
the word you, with the 'll a link to the indicator

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to respond and gloating that another will be found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get caught' signals one word held inside a phrase; the surface reads as a taunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'never you mind' is a brush-off meaning the speaker declines to reply.

clue.text: Exploit them, if weaker? That's out of order!

indicators.note: out of order means not in proper sequence, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of the vulnerable is unacceptable behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges THEM IF WEAKER, and it also sounds like an outraged verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: To make free with something is to use it as if one's own, taking advantage.

clue.text: Reported seal — one seen swimming near pen

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a ring

explanation.surface: A news item about a seal sighted near a fish pen or enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' suggests an enclosure, but a pen is a female swan, whose young swims beside her.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is a female swan, and her young one swimming alongside is a baby swan.

clue.text: It could be one's turn to make an entrance

definitions.text: It could be one's turn to make an entrance

parts.words: It could be one's turn to make an entrance
parts.note: reads like an actor awaiting a cue, but it is the handle you turn to open a door and go in

explanation.surface: An actor in the wings waiting for the moment to go on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A round door handle is turned to open the door, which lets you enter a room.

clue.text: Writer held back by fat cat

indicators.note: the reversed name is held inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking

indicators.note: back says the writer's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: An author restrained by an overweight, greedy rich man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' and 'back' are separate signals: the writer is turned round and held in the fat. 'fat cat' reads as one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: The leopard is one of the big cats, a spotted wild member of the cat family.

clue.text: Fix up accomodation for possibly heartless food supplier

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue up means read upward, reversed

parts.note: to nail is to fix in place

indicators.note: heartless means losing the middle letter

parts.note: maybe means possibly

explanation.surface: Repair housing for a cruel caterer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NAIL to LIAN; 'heartless' takes Y from MAYBE to give MABE, which LIAN houses ('accomodation for'). The clue misspells accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A lima bean is an edible legume, a plant source of food.

clue.text: A fit of anger, in essence

parts.note: a as in 'ten pounds a head' means per
to be in a fume is to be in a rage

explanation.surface: Someone flaring into a temper over the heart of a matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' stands for PER, as in 'so much a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence is a word for scent, an extracted fragrant oil, so a fragrance.

clue.text: Half of messengers run off what's to be posted in here?

definitions.text: what's to be posted in here?

indicators.note: half the word is taken off

parts.note: envoys are messengers
to elope is to run off to marry

explanation.surface: Some of the couriers abscond with the outgoing mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' keeps ENV from ENVOYS.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter is posted inside a paper cover sealed and addressed for the mail.

clue.text: Is about to break sets of dishes? Overfilled glass shows it!

indicators.note: breaking into a word means going inside it

parts.note: menus list a restaurant's sets of dishes
taken as written
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A clumsy diner smashes crockery and a brimming glass.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa) is the standard abbreviation for about; 'to break' signals going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A brim-full glass shows a curved liquid surface bulging above the rim.

clue.text: Optional extra for facade, in such traditional style

definitions.text: Optional extra for facade, in such traditional style

parts.words: Optional extra for facade, in such traditional style
parts.note: reads like an architectural add-on, but it is the hook under the c of the French-style spelling, which may be kept or dropped

explanation.surface: An extra flourish one may add to a building's front in a classic manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Facade is often written with a hooked mark under the c, which English spelling may omit.

clue.text: Dubious creed — I'm adopting nothing second-rate

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the zero goes inside
dubious means suspect, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: I'm gives the letters IM
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone doubting a set of beliefs, embracing nihilism, judged inferior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dubious' gives the anagram MEDICRE, and 'adopting' takes the zero into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocre means of only middling quality, not good enough, which is second-rate.

clue.text: Believe it's on the cards?

definitions.meaning: to ... a claim is to believe it
a ... card carries a spending allowance

explanation.surface: Trusting that something is likely to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit means trust a statement, and a credit card offers borrowing.

clue.text: Compete with woman about to make capital

parts.note: to vie is to compete

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the name is reversed

parts.note: Ann, a woman's name

explanation.surface: A rivalry with a woman over making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ANN to NNA; 'capital' looks like money but is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria.

clue.text: Having difference at home, left, being put up by fine Scottish relation

indicators.note: being put up means being housed, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: braw is Scots for fine or good
to have difference is to be other, different
at home is in

explanation.surface: A Scot puts up an awkward in-law after a family row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being put up by' means housed inside; braw is a Scots word, so 'Scottish' belongs to the wordplay, not the relation.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother-in-law is a relative by marriage, so a relation.

clue.text: In dispute over first of openers given not out

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the next word
out signals the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Arguing about a cricket opener's reprieve by the umpire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges NOT into NTO after the O picked by 'first of'. To be on to someone about something is to keep pressing or nagging them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on to someone about a matter means pestering them over it, in contention.

clue.text: Start off easy task, but make slow progress

indicators.note: the start of the word comes off

parts.note: a cinch is something easily done

explanation.surface: Begin an easy job but advance only gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' removes the C of CINCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to move forward very slowly, a little at a time.

clue.text: Receiver's about right for such an important channel

indicators.note: about means around, so the receiver goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: an aerial receives broadcast signals; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A radio aerial correctly positioned for an important broadcast channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means around; the channel is a main road or blood vessel, not a TV station.
explanation.definitionFit: An arterial road or vessel is a main route, which suits a major channel.

clue.text: One showing sparkling facets of some drama met hysteria

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stage play's glittering sides meet with overwrought reactions.
explanation.definitionFit: This purple gemstone is cut with facets that sparkle.
